candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record documents multifocal osteomyelitis (scapula and distal tibia), so 'Osteomyelitis, multifocal' is anatomically and morphologically compatible. However, the benchmark requires identification of Cryptococcus as the causative organism. The clinical context strongly suggests a fungal etiology — the patient failed 6 months of anti-tubercular therapy, had negative sputum studies, and presented with progressive multifocal bone lesions — pointing to an opportunistic pathogen such as Cryptococcus rather than mycobacteria. The candidate label captures the parent/descriptive category but lacks the required etiologic specificity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Describes the anatomical pattern (multifocal osteomyelitis involving scapula and distal tibia) but omits the specific etiologic agent (Cryptococcus), which is the essential distinguishing component of the benchmark diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Etiologic confirmation (culture/histopathology) pending at time of presentation; diagnosis of Cryptococcal osteomyelitis is clinically inferred from failure of anti-tubercular therapy and multifocal bone involvement pattern
